title: The lavan as a map
hookLine: duty, fearlessness, longing and union: the four rounds as the stages of a marriage
tomorrow: the Granth says some couples only sit together. who?

lines: MARIGOLDS, TRAYS, A DUPATTA ON A LAMP.
cards: The morning after the wedding, the house is wrecked in the happiest way: marigolds on the stairs, a mountain of steel trays by the sink, somebody's dupatta hanging from a lamp.
Jasleen and Aman stop by Bebe's on their way to Aman's parents' place. Jasleen has a folded printout of the lavan in English that the granthi gave them, already covered in pen.
She sets it on the kitchen table in front of Bebe and taps the four verses one by one. Bebe, which one are we in?

teach.h: THE SOUL'S JOURNEY, AS A MAP FOR TWO.
teach.b: Bebe puts on her glasses. The lavan, by Guru Ram Das on ang 773 and 774, describe a soul's journey to God, told as a bride's journey to her husband.

Some couples also read them as a map for two, and Bebe reads them that way now, in paraphrase. The first round is about duty: taking up the life of a householder, with the Name and right living as its ground.

teach.h: ONE: DUTY. TWO: FEAR FALLS AWAY.
teach.b: The second is about fear falling away, the meeting with the True Guru that leaves the heart unafraid.
The third is about longing, a love that wants God more than anything the world hands you. The fourth is sahaj, ease and peace, the union, where the mind settles at last. Then Bebe gives her answer.
You're in the first one, beta. Rent, groceries, a job to find, your mother-in-law's kitchen rules. That's not the boring round.
It's the ground the other three stand on.
Aman laughs for the first time in a week. And Bebe says one more thing: a map doesn't mean you walk it once. Some days you'll be back in the first round, some days you'll get a glimpse of the fourth.

how: Sikh couples and families sometimes study the four lavan together before or after the Anand Karaj, reading them both as the soul's journey to God and as guidance for married life.

games.q: what does “the lavan as a map” mean?
o: a list of four rules a couple must follow
the four wedding verses read as stages of a life
the route the wedding party walks to the gurdwara

games.q: four rounds, four stages — tap the pairs.

s: the lavan are only about the couple's relationship
they describe the soul's journey to God; some couples also read them as a map for two.
in Bebe's reading, the first round is the boring one to get past
it's the ground the other three stand on: rent, groceries, a job to find.
the fourth round speaks of sahaj, ease and peace
the union, where the mind settles.

games.q: your married friend says, 'we used to feel the fourth round. now it's all bills and chores. did we lose it?' what does Bebe's map say?
o: a map isn't walked once; you circle back to duty, and you glimpse ease again.
yes; once you leave the fourth round, it doesn't come back.
bills and chores mean you were never in the fourth round at all.
games.why: Bebe: some days you'll be back in the first round, some days you'll glimpse the fourth. the first round is ground, not failure.

practice: If you can, stand and take four slow steps, one for each round, feeling each foot land. Then sit down again and ask yourself quietly which round your own life feels like this week: duty, fear falling away, longing, or ease.
Name it, without grading it, and rest there for the sit.

wordCard.voice: The lavan as a map. The four wedding verses, read as the stages of a shared life: duty, fearlessness, longing and union.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sahaj, ease and inner peace, named in the fourth lav.

carryVoice: A map for two, and the first round is the ground the other three stand on. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Ang 773–774 (Raag Suhi, Chhant, Guru Ram Das: the four lavan), paraphrased
